title: From the cracks of the earth (Kern ch. 14)
word: From the cracks of the earth
hookLine: countless bodhisattvas rise from the ground, pupils of the Buddha from long ago
tomorrow: The lifespan of the Tathagata (Kern ch. 15)

cards: In spring, a crack in the sidewalk fills with green. Nobody planted it or watered it. It was down there all along, working in the dark, and one day it's just up.

Chapter fourteen of the Lotus Sutra opens with an offer of help. Bodhisattvas from other worlds say to the Buddha: let us protect this sutra here after you're gone. A generous offer, and a sensible one.
The Buddha turns it down. No need, he says. This world already has its own.
Then the ground starts to split.

teach.b: First, the refusal. The visitors mean well, but this world has bodhisattvas of its own who will keep the sutra after him.
Second, the earth opens. All across this world the ground cracks, and up rise bodhisattvas beyond counting, bodies shining gold, each with a great company of followers.

They go up to the jeweled stupa still hanging in the sky and bow to the two Buddhas seated there. Four lead them, and all four names speak of conduct: superior, boundless, pure, and firm. Third, nobody knows them.
Maitreya, who is said to be the next Buddha, has never seen a single one, and neither has anyone else. Who are these?
The Buddha answers: I taught them, all of them, here in this world since my awakening. They've lived below, studying quietly, away from crowds. Fourth, the puzzle.
Maitreya is honest about how strange that sounds. You awakened not long ago; how could you have taught so many?

teach.h: A YOUNG MAN WITH OLD SONS.
teach.b: It's like a young man with dark hair pointing at white-haired elders and saying, these are my sons, while they nod and say, he's our father. Who would believe it?
The chapter ends with that question in the air, and tomorrow answers it.

This is the week's last day, so lay its chapters side by side: the attendant and the son, the one who teaches a single verse, a girl from under the sea, two women waiting to be named, and now a crowd nobody knew was there.
All week, the Lotus kept counting the people nobody was counting.

how: In Mahayana communities that read the Lotus Sutra, the bodhisattvas who rise from the earth are honored as the ones entrusted with the sutra in this world, and some schools, including Nichiren Buddhism, give them and their leader a central place.

games.q: what does “from the cracks of the earth” mean?
o: spirits of the dead who return to hear the Buddha
visitors from other worlds sent to guard the sutra
countless bodhisattvas this world already had, rising up

games.q: they rose from the earth: tap the pairs.
p: offer to protect the sutra here
says no need: this world has its own
has never seen any of them

s: the Buddha gladly accepts the visitors' help
he turns it down: this world, he says, has bodhisattvas of its own.
the new bodhisattvas come down from the sky
they rise up from beneath the earth, which cracks open across the world.
Maitreya doesn't recognize a single one of them
nobody in the assembly has seen them before, so he asks who they are.

games.q: you're Maitreya. the Buddha says he taught every one of these countless bodhisattvas. what do you say?
o: how? it's like a young man calling old men his sons.
nothing: you don't question the Buddha.
games.why: Maitreya says it plainly: a young man with dark hair, white-haired elders calling him father. who'd believe it? tomorrow's chapter answers.

practice: Feel the ground holding you up, and bring to mind one thing in your life that grew while nobody was watching: a friendship that deepened without a big moment, a child suddenly taller, a patience you didn't have a few years ago.
Notice how long it was working underground before it showed, and rest with it.

wordCard.voice: From the cracks of the earth. Bodhisattvas beyond counting, taught by the Buddha in this world, rise from beneath it when he says no outside help is needed. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: a being set on awakening, like the ones who rise from the earth in chapter fourteen.

carryVoice: Your line: they rose from the earth. Nobody knew they were there. I'll be here tomorrow.
